title: NO DEPTH TEST of StandardMaterial3d of stencil outline works on the editor but not when the game is run
body: ### Tested versions -Reproducible in v4.7.beta3.official [860821708] and v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] ### System information Godot v4.7.beta3 - Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) 13 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 550 / 550 Series (radeonsi, polaris12, ACO, DRM 3.61, 6.12.74+deb13+1-amd64) - AMD Ryzen 5 4500 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.49 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description The goal is creating an outline of a 3d Meshinstance using the StandardMaterial3d stencil method. This outline is supposed to be visible through walls by turning on the NO DEPTH TEST flag on the StandardMaterial3d of the next pass material which is generated by the stencil outline. After turning on "NO DEPTH TEST" , the outline can be visible through walls on the godot editor. The outline is not visible through walls when the game is run. Reloading the project will turn off the "NO DEPTH TEST" flag of the stencil outline which was on previously before the reload, requiring you to turn it on again for it to work only on the godot editor. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Add 2 meshinstances to your scene. 2. The first meshinstance is a small cube that we will add an outline to. Add a cube mesh on your meshinstance. 3. The second meshinstance is a larger cube that will be used as an obstacle which sit infront of the small cube from the editor or game camera. We should be able to see the outline of the small cube through this larger cube after setting up the outline. The smaller cube should not be inside the larger one unless culling is disabled on the larger obstacle. 4. Lets setup the small cube outline : Create a StandardMaterial3D for your small cube mesh. Give it an albedo color or texture.Go to stencil of the StandardMaterial3D, set the mode to outline and adjust thickness of the outline to a visible one. Give the outline a colour. 5. On the next pass property, expand the StandardMaterial3D and the transparency should be "alpha". Depth draw mode should be "never" and no_depth_test should be set on to be able to render infront of obscuring objects. -The cube's outline should be able to render infront of the larger obstacle 6. Setup a camera3d where the larger obstacle is infront of the camera and obscuring the small obstacle. Run the game and notice that the cube outline is rendered behind the larger obstacle however we intended the outline to be rendered through obstacles. Final Test : -Lets try reloading the project in the project tab. Once the scene that we set up opens up, notice how the no_depth_test of the stencil outline is disabled? You need to re-enable no_depth_test again on the "next pass" property of the small cubes standard_material3d CONCLUSION: -no_depth_test of the stencil only works in the editor & not in the game. -no_depth_test of the stencil outline material disables after reloading the game project. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Minimum reproduction project : [stencil_no_depth_test_issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28296915/stencil_no_depth_test_issue.zip) The project setup has been explained through Label3Ds. Having explained to the best of my experiences on the issue, please let me know if anything needs clarification.
